part1_level3b.why: The map ends on ::rails::train::end_trigger, a DYNAMIC OBJECT armed by the train FSM (do_enablecollisions(true) @25649012; the camera7 block @25543652 starts its move animation). Its DO_CharacterCollides table (@24214363) holds three strings: two do_enablecollisions(false) (@24214524, @24214656) and maxpayne_gamemode->gm_init(part1_level4) @24214718; the second is another handler, not part of the same line list. The player fires it by jumping from the roof edge onto the following train (walkthroughs, out/bec/s1104/S_result.md); standing still it never fires, on native either (Q_result.md). ::rails::old kills the player on collision @24212125, so the tp ::rails::w3 is the protection. The jump is real play (WORKLIST #7), so the route injects that DO's own two lines verbatim, 30 s after jump_trigger (cutscene ~6 s + the armed train pass ~25 s): the level's own exit actions at the moment the level would run them, not a skip of its content. 7 native jump tries (out/q3b/chela_t1..t7) did not land the collision.

part1_level4.why: Level ends by itself on the last kill: ::end::end_timer FSM needs 3 'add' (FSM_Send) and then runs end_timer.DO->DO_Animate(timer) @26884131; end_timer.DO does graphicnovel + gm_init(part1_level5) @28456850. Adds come from ::end::death_counter (::end::e1..e4 die @26977862..), ::end::death_counter3 (::teleport::e1..e3 die @26989249..) and ::startroom::gognitti (OnDeath-style add @26988695; its record also sets invulnerable, so the add may only fire on a scripted end). First wave death -> second_wave_trigger1 trigger_me -> ::end::script3 initialize teleports ::teleport::e1..e3 in (@26888889). No 'send': fleet s1104b put gm_init(part1_level5) at 103 s, before the exit step, and the DO->DO_Animate line queued at 107 s was parsed at 142 s with the level already part1_level5 (page.tail 142.2), where the name is absent; X_Message::parse reports that miss as a 'Receiver class' (the name falls through to the Class:Id form, and '::end::end_timer.DO' is no class) and the SEH wrapper closes the game. The '.DO' name is a per-level scope-table key, so no exits.json field keeps a queued line inside its level: the kill list is the lever. Keep first-wave e1..e4 in the final objective too: rescuing second_wave_trigger1 does not kill them or satisfy death_counter (@26977862), and the exit still needs its add. The exact call is ::end::end_timer.DO->DO_Animate(timer) @26884131, animation name timer @28456455, and ::startroom::gognitti is invulnerable until @28446593.

part3_level4.why: Exit-only route (2026-11-02, scratchpad tools/exitscan.py over the .ldb): the record that sends gm_init(next) and its sender. 'send' lines are copied verbatim from the .ldb (a receiver the level lacks closes the game). ::3::trigger01 starts inactive (fleet chain2: T_Activate did nothing); its own actions are sent instead. Only the first line: fleet s1104b sent both in one batch, DO_Animate(1) resolved in part3_level4 at 44.0 s and gm_init(part3_level5) followed at 45.0 s, and the queued CAM_AttachToDO line was then parsed at 83.2 s inside part3_level5 (page.tail 83.2) where ::3::cam_end.DO does not exist, which closed the game. The mailbox runs one line per input read, so a two-line batch cannot land in one level. The chain found in the .ldb: ::3::trigger01's active step (@26246238) holds ::3::look.TRIGGER->t_enable(false), cam_end.DO->DO_Animate(1) @26246276 and cam_end.DO->CAM_AttachToDO(1, false) @26246310, and ::booth::wait.DO's step @27962064 (the phone) switches trigger01 active @27962191 and enables ::3::look.TRIGGER @27962229, so the map's own way in is a trigger, not a queued message. The send omits ::3::cam_end.DO->CAM_AttachToDO(1, false) @26246309 because one line lands per level.
